decision: Treat XRP's CFTC digital-commodity classification, Deribit venue collateral eligibility, CFM product enablement and actual collateral use as four separate evidence states.
rules: Record CFTC Letter 26-17 as a conditional staff no-action position and interpretation, not a binding rule or universal authorization.
Record XRP as explicitly named in the digital-commodity examples in CFTC Letter 26-17 footnote 5.
Record Deribit's September 28 table as current venue evidence: XRP is a full cross-collateral currency and offset currency; X:PM has no stated haircut and X:SM has a 15% haircut.
Do not use the January 13 Deribit update saying XRP remained offset-only as current; it is superseded by the September 28 cross-collateral table.
Do not infer that CFM has enabled XRP collateral until its notice/commencement date, three-month initial restriction, U.S. product eligibility and customer account settings are verified.
Do not infer that collateral posting creates a new spot purchase. Track pre-existing holdings, new deposits, collateral balances, re-use and spot acquisitions separately.
Track rehypothecation/right-of-reuse as both a capital-efficiency channel and a counterparty/custody risk.
Keep venue haircut, FCM capital charge, DCO/foreign clearing margin and liquidation threshold as separate numeric fields.
No predictive feature admission until actual collateral balances and source timestamps are independently corroborated.
